```{python}
# | tags: [setup]
import os
from pathlib import Path

import anndata as ad
import matplotlib.colors as mcolors
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import scanpy as sc
import numpy as np
import pandas as pd
from mpl_toolkits.axes_grid1 import make_axes_locatable
from scipy.stats import kruskal, rankdata

# Phase C's low count cut. Phase B draws it as a marker so the plots show what it would
# remove; nothing is filtered here.
LOW_COUNT_CUT = 20

# Phase D: the reference's cell types, germ first, and the colours the figures draw them in.
GERM = ["SPG", "Scytes", "STids", "Elongating"]
SOMATIC = ["Sertoli", "Leydig", "Myoid", "Endothelial", "Macrophage", "InnateLymph", "Unknown"]
CELL_TYPES = GERM + SOMATIC
TYPE_COLORS = {
    "SPG": "#1f77b4", "Scytes": "#2ca02c", "STids": "#ff7f0e", "Elongating": "#d62728",
    "Sertoli": "#9467bd", "Leydig": "#000000", "Myoid": "#e377c2", "Endothelial": "#17becf",
    "Macrophage": "#8c564b", "InnateLymph": "#bcbd22", "Unknown": "#7f7f7f",
}
GROUP_COLORS = {"germ": "#d98c1f", "somatic": "#4a7fb5"}

# Phase D6: the twelve germ-cell clusters, coloured along one ramp so neighbours look alike.
GC_TYPES = [f"GC{i}" for i in range(1, 13)]
GC_COLORS = {gc: mcolors.to_hex(plt.cm.turbo(0.05 + 0.9 * i / 11)) for i, gc in enumerate(GC_TYPES)}
GC_COLORS["not germ"] = "#d9d9d9"

# Phases G and H: the stage groups Alex Vargo staged tubules into, and the mosaic pixel size his
# tubule areas are in.
STAGE_GROUPS = ["1-3", "4-6", "7-8", "9-12"]
UM_PER_PX = 0.108

# The repository root, where the cached reference lives. A render outside the
# repository sets MERFISH_REPO.
_start = Path(os.environ["MERFISH_REPO"]) if "MERFISH_REPO" in os.environ else Path.cwd()
REPO = next(p for p in [_start, *_start.parents] if (p / "PLAN.md").exists())
REFERENCE_DIR = REPO / "results/section_analysis/reference"

# What the workflow staged beside the notebook, told apart by file name suffix. The trailing
# comma raises unless exactly one matches.
(TABLE,) = Path(".").glob("*.create_spatialdata_cellpose.h5ad")
(FOV_EXTENTS,) = Path(".").glob("*.fov_extents.csv")
# Phase E: Alex Vargo's tubule results for the section, a map from each cell to its tubule and a
# table per tubule. A section's metadata file may be the "-staged" one.
(TUBULE_MAP,) = Path(".").glob("*cell-to-tubule-map-goodcells.npz")
(TUBULE_META,) = Path(".").glob("*tubule-metadata*.csv")
```

```{python}
# | tags: [helpers]
# Plotting only: every function here takes already-computed data and draws a figure.
# No AnnData indexing, aggregation or column derivation happens in this cell.


def plot_counts_per_cell(transcripts, genes, medians, low_cut, share_below_cut):
    """B2: transcripts per cell and genes per cell, as histograms over the full range."""
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(9, 3.4), constrained_layout=True)
    panels = [
        (transcripts, "Transcripts per cell", "transcripts", 8, True),
        (genes, "Genes per cell", "genes", 2, False),
    ]
    for ax, (x, title, name, width, mark_cut) in zip(axes, panels):
        # Integer-aligned bins: each holds the same number of whole counts, so there is
        # no comb pattern.
        ax.hist(x, bins=np.arange(-0.5, x.max() + width, width), color="0.35")
        ax.axvline(medians[name], color="tab:blue", lw=1.2, label=f"median {medians[name]:.0f}")
        if mark_cut:
            ax.axvline(
                low_cut,
                color="tab:red",
                lw=1.2,
                ls="--",
                label=f"Phase C cut ({low_cut}): {share_below_cut:.1%} of cells",
            )
        ax.set(title=title, xlabel=f"{name} per cell", ylabel="cells")
        ax.legend(frameon=False, fontsize=8)
    return fig


def plot_cell_volume(volume, median, bin_width=20):
    """B3: cell volume, as a histogram over the full range."""
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(4.8, 3.4), constrained_layout=True)
    ax.hist(volume, bins=np.arange(0, volume.max() + bin_width, bin_width), color="0.35")
    ax.axvline(median, color="tab:blue", lw=1.2, label=f"median {median:.0f} µm³")
    ax.set(title="Cell volume", xlabel="volume (µm³)", ylabel="cells")
    ax.legend(frameon=False, fontsize=8)
    return fig


def plot_blank_codewords(gene_totals, blank_totals, cells_per_blank_count):
    """B4: blank codewords against real genes, per codeword and per cell."""
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(9, 3.4), constrained_layout=True)
    rng = np.random.default_rng(0)

    # Left: one dot per codeword, jittered sideways, with each group's median.
    ax = axes[0]
    groups = [(gene_totals, "0.35", "real genes"), (blank_totals, "tab:red", "blank codewords")]
    for x_, (totals, color, name) in enumerate(groups):
        ax.scatter(x_ + rng.uniform(-0.3, 0.3, len(totals)), totals, s=6, color=color, alpha=0.7, linewidths=0)
        ax.hlines(np.median(totals), x_ - 0.38, x_ + 0.38, color="tab:blue", lw=1.5)
    ax.set_yscale("log")
    ax.set_xticks([0, 1], [f"real genes (n={len(gene_totals)})", f"blank codewords (n={len(blank_totals)})"])
    ax.set(title="Total counts per codeword", ylabel="counts across the section (log)", xlim=(-0.6, 1.6))

    # Right: how many cells have 0, 1, 2, ... blank counts; the first few are labelled.
    ax = axes[1]
    k = np.arange(len(cells_per_blank_count))
    ax.bar(k, cells_per_blank_count, width=0.9, color="0.35")
    for x_ in k[:4]:
        ax.text(x_, cells_per_blank_count[x_], f"{cells_per_blank_count[x_] / cells_per_blank_count.sum():.0%}",
                ha="center", va="bottom", fontsize=7)
    ax.set(title="Blank counts per cell", xlabel="blank counts in the cell", ylabel="cells")
    return fig


def plot_transcripts_on_tissue(xy, transcripts, vmax, x_profile, y_profile, x_bounds, y_bounds):
    """B5: transcript count drawn on tissue, with its mean along x and y at the margins.

    x_bounds and y_bounds are where the field-of-view columns and rows start and end.
    """
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 7), constrained_layout=True)
    pts = ax.scatter(xy[:, 0], xy[:, 1], c=transcripts, s=0.4, cmap="viridis", vmin=0, vmax=vmax,
                     linewidths=0, rasterized=True)
    ax.set_aspect("equal")
    ax.invert_yaxis()
    ax.set(xlabel="x (µm)", ylabel="y (µm)")

    divider = make_axes_locatable(ax)
    ax_top = divider.append_axes("top", size="22%", pad=0.08, sharex=ax)
    ax_right = divider.append_axes("right", size="22%", pad=0.08, sharey=ax)
    cax = divider.append_axes("bottom", size="3%", pad=0.65)

    ax_top.plot(*x_profile, color="0.2", lw=0.8)
    for b in x_bounds:
        ax_top.axvline(b, color="red", lw=0.4, alpha=0.4)
    ax_top.set(ylabel="mean per cell")
    ax_top.tick_params(labelbottom=False)
    ax_top.set_title("Transcripts per cell on tissue")

    ax_right.plot(y_profile[1], y_profile[0], color="0.2", lw=0.8)
    for b in y_bounds:
        ax_right.axhline(b, color="red", lw=0.4, alpha=0.4)
    ax_right.set(xlabel="mean per cell")
    ax_right.tick_params(labelleft=False)

    fig.colorbar(pts, cax=cax, orientation="horizontal",
                 label=f"transcripts per cell (colour clipped at the 99th percentile, {vmax:.0f})")
    return fig


def plot_pca_variance(variance_ratio, sample):
    """C4: variance explained by each principal component."""
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(5, 3.2), constrained_layout=True)
    ax.plot(np.arange(1, len(variance_ratio) + 1), variance_ratio, "o-", ms=3, color="0.3")
    ax.set(title=f"{sample}: variance explained per PC", xlabel="PC", ylabel="variance ratio")
    return fig


def plot_umap_by_count(umap, transcripts, vmax, sample):
    """C6: UMAP coloured by transcript count, low counts drawn first."""
    order = np.argsort(transcripts)
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6, 5.5), constrained_layout=True)
    pts = ax.scatter(umap[order, 0], umap[order, 1], c=transcripts[order], s=0.3, cmap="viridis",
                     vmax=vmax, linewidths=0, rasterized=True)
    fig.colorbar(pts, label="transcripts per cell (colour clipped at the 99th percentile)")
    ax.set(title=f"{sample}: UMAP by transcript count", xlabel="UMAP1", ylabel="UMAP2")
    return fig


def plot_shared_genes(n_panel, n_shared):
    """D3: how many of the panel's genes the reference has."""
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(4.8, 2.4), constrained_layout=True)
    ax.barh(["panel genes", "shared with\nthe reference"], [n_panel, n_shared], color=["0.65", "0.3"])
    for y, n in enumerate([n_panel, n_shared]):
        ax.text(n, y, f" {n}", va="center")
    ax.set(xlim=(0, n_panel * 1.12), xlabel="genes")
    ax.invert_yaxis()
    return fig


def plot_calls(umap, xy, calls, colors, sample, what, last=()):
    """D5: a per-cell label on the UMAP and on the tissue. Labels in `last` are drawn on top."""
    calls = np.asarray(calls)
    on_top = np.isin(calls, list(last))
    order = np.r_[np.random.default_rng(0).permutation(np.flatnonzero(~on_top)), np.flatnonzero(on_top)]
    point_colors = np.array([colors[k] for k in calls])

    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(15, 6.5), constrained_layout=True)
    axes[0].scatter(umap[order, 0], umap[order, 1], c=point_colors[order], s=0.3, linewidths=0, rasterized=True)
    axes[0].set(title=f"{sample}: {what} on UMAP", xticks=[], yticks=[])
    axes[1].scatter(xy[order, 0], xy[order, 1], c=point_colors[order], s=0.5, linewidths=0, rasterized=True)
    axes[1].set_aspect("equal")
    axes[1].invert_yaxis()
    axes[1].set(title=f"{sample}: {what} on tissue", xlabel="x (µm)", ylabel="y (µm)")
    for label, color in colors.items():
        if (calls == label).any():
            axes[1].scatter([], [], c=color, s=25, label=f"{label} ({(calls == label).sum():,})")
    axes[1].legend(frameon=False, fontsize=8, loc="upper left", bbox_to_anchor=(1, 1))
    return fig


def plot_tubules_on_tissue(xy, tubule_codes, is_germ, sample):
    """E3: each tubule in its own colour; somatic cells outside any tubule grey, germ cells outside black."""
    inside = tubule_codes >= 0
    colors = np.random.default_rng(5).uniform(0.1, 0.95, (tubule_codes.max() + 1, 3))
    outside_somatic, outside_germ = ~inside & ~is_germ, ~inside & is_germ

    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(11, 9.3), constrained_layout=True)
    ax.scatter(xy[outside_somatic, 0], xy[outside_somatic, 1], c="0.8", s=0.4, linewidths=0, rasterized=True)
    ax.scatter(xy[inside, 0], xy[inside, 1], c=colors[tubule_codes[inside]], s=0.5, linewidths=0, rasterized=True)
    ax.scatter(xy[outside_germ, 0], xy[outside_germ, 1], c="k", s=1.5, linewidths=0, rasterized=True)
    ax.set_aspect("equal")
    ax.invert_yaxis()
    ax.set(title=f"{sample}: {tubule_codes.max() + 1} tubules; {outside_germ.sum():,} germ cells outside any (black)",
           xlabel="x (µm)", ylabel="y (µm)")
    return fig


def plot_tubule_qc(cells_per_tubule, share_inside):
    """E3: cells per tubule, and the share of each cell type that falls inside a tubule."""
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(11, 3.8), constrained_layout=True)
    axes[0].hist(cells_per_tubule, bins=40, color="0.35")
    axes[0].axvline(np.median(cells_per_tubule), color="tab:blue", lw=1.2,
                    label=f"median {np.median(cells_per_tubule):.0f}")
    axes[0].set(title="Cells per tubule", xlabel="cells", ylabel="tubules")
    axes[0].legend(frameon=False, fontsize=8)
    axes[1].barh(share_inside.index, share_inside.to_numpy(), color="0.35")
    axes[1].invert_yaxis()
    axes[1].set(title="Share of each cell type inside a tubule", xlabel="share of cells", xlim=(0, 1))
    return fig


def plot_stage_composition(mean_composition, tubules_per_group, sample):
    """H1: the mean cell-type composition of a tubule at each stage group, as stacked bars."""
    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7.5, 5), constrained_layout=True)
    bottom = np.zeros(len(mean_composition))
    for cell_type in mean_composition.columns:
        share = mean_composition[cell_type].to_numpy()
        ax.bar(range(len(share)), share, bottom=bottom, color=TYPE_COLORS[cell_type], label=cell_type, width=0.7)
        bottom += share
    ax.set_xticks(range(len(mean_composition)),
                  [f"{g}\n(n={tubules_per_group[g]})" for g in mean_composition.index])
    ax.set(title=f"{sample}: cell-type composition of tubules by stage", xlabel="stage group",
           ylabel="share of cells in the tubule", ylim=(0, 1))
    ax.legend(frameon=False, fontsize=8, loc="upper left", bbox_to_anchor=(1.01, 1))
    return fig


def plot_stage_density(density, stage, columns, sample):
    """H2: cells per 10,000 µm² of tubule outline at each stage group, one panel per column."""
    fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 3, figsize=(12, 6.5), constrained_layout=True)
    for ax, column in zip(axes.ravel(), columns):
        groups = [density.loc[stage == g, column] for g in STAGE_GROUPS]
        ax.boxplot(groups, tick_labels=STAGE_GROUPS, showfliers=False, patch_artist=True,
                   boxprops=dict(facecolor=TYPE_COLORS.get(column, "0.6"), alpha=0.6),
                   medianprops=dict(color="k"))
        ax.set(title=column, ylabel="cells per 10,000 µm²")
    fig.suptitle(f"{sample}: cell density in the tubule by stage (n = "
                 + ", ".join(f"{g}: {int((stage == g).sum())}" for g in STAGE_GROUPS) + ")")
    return fig
```

## B1. Load the section

The table is Phase A's output: raw counts for the 491 panel genes in `X`, per-cell
segmentation metadata in `obs`, and the blank codewords kept apart in `obsm["blank"]`. The
raw counts are copied to a layer, because normalization later overwrites `X`. The table
has neither a transcript count nor a gene count, so both are derived here, over the real
genes only; blank codewords are not counted. `transcript_count` is a cell's total counts
and `gene_count` is how many genes it has at least one count for.

```{python}
adata = ad.read_h5ad(TABLE)

# The sample id comes from inside the object, never from the staged file name.
assert adata.obs["sample"].nunique() == 1, "one table must hold exactly one sample"
SAMPLE = str(adata.obs["sample"].iat[0])

adata.layers["counts"] = adata.X.copy()
# C1 drops cells, and a per-cell file from outside is indexed by the full table: keep each cell's row.
adata.obs["table_row"] = np.arange(adata.n_obs)
N_TABLE_CELLS = adata.n_obs
adata.obs["transcript_count"] = np.asarray(adata.layers["counts"].sum(axis=1)).ravel()
adata.obs["gene_count"] = np.asarray((adata.layers["counts"] > 0).sum(axis=1)).ravel()

print(f"{SAMPLE}: {adata.n_obs:,} cells x {adata.n_vars} genes")
```

## B2. Transcripts and genes per cell

How deeply each cell was read. The red line is Phase C's low count cut; it only marks what
that cut would remove. The x-axis runs to each distribution's maximum, so the sparse high
tail is on the plot.

```{python}
transcripts = adata.obs["transcript_count"]
genes = adata.obs["gene_count"]

medians = {"transcripts": np.median(transcripts), "genes": np.median(genes)}
share_below_cut = (transcripts < LOW_COUNT_CUT).mean()

plot_counts_per_cell(transcripts, genes, medians, LOW_COUNT_CUT, share_below_cut)
plt.show()
print(f"maximum: {transcripts.max():.0f} transcripts, {genes.max()} genes")
```

## B3. Cell volume

How large the segmented cells are. A fragment would show as a cluster of very small cells,
and a merge of two cells as a cluster of very large ones. `volume` is in cubic micrometres;
the table's `volume_voxels` is the same measure in voxels, at 0.0175 µm³ per voxel. Nothing
is cut on volume.

```{python}
volume = adata.obs["volume"]

plot_cell_volume(volume, volume.median())
plt.show()
print(f"range: {volume.min():.1f} to {volume.max():.0f} µm³")
```

## B4. Blank codewords against real genes

Blank codewords are probes that should never bind anything, so the counts they collect are
the noise floor. The left panel puts each blank codeword beside each real gene by its total
counts across the section, and shows how far the genes sit above the blanks and whether any
single blank stands out. The right panel shows how many blank counts a single cell
collects, which is how much stray signal one cell carries. Both are looked at, not cut on.

```{python}
blank = adata.obsm["blank"]

gene_totals = np.asarray(adata.layers["counts"].sum(axis=0)).ravel()
blank_totals = blank.sum(axis=0).to_numpy()
blank_per_cell = blank.sum(axis=1).to_numpy()
cells_per_blank_count = np.bincount(blank_per_cell.astype(int))

plot_blank_codewords(gene_totals, blank_totals, cells_per_blank_count)
plt.show()

blank_share = blank_per_cell.sum() / (blank_per_cell.sum() + adata.obs["transcript_count"].sum())
print(f"blank codewords are {blank_share:.2%} of all counts")
print(
    f"median codeword: {np.median(gene_totals):.0f} counts for real genes, "
    f"{np.median(blank_totals):.0f} for blanks ({np.median(gene_totals) / np.median(blank_totals):.1f}x)"
)
for label, cut in [("median", np.median(blank_totals)), ("95th percentile", np.quantile(blank_totals, 0.95))]:
    print(f"real genes below the blank {label} ({cut:.0f}): {(gene_totals < cut).sum()} of {len(gene_totals)}")
```

## B5. Transcript count on tissue

Where in the section cells were read poorly. Each dot is a cell, coloured by its transcript
count. The curves on the top and right edges are the mean transcripts per cell along x and
along y, in 10 µm bins; they share the map's axes, so a dip sits directly over the part of the
tissue it comes from. The red lines on the curves are where the imaging fields of view's
columns and rows start and end. Where the mean dips on a line, cells along that
field-of-view boundary were read less deeply; a wide, smooth fall towards the border of the
tissue is a different thing, the edge. Nothing is cut on either.

```{python}
xy = np.asarray(adata.obsm["spatial"])
transcripts = adata.obs["transcript_count"].to_numpy()


def mean_by_bin(coord, values, width=10, min_cells=20):
    """Mean of values in bins along one axis; bins with too few cells are left blank."""
    edges = np.arange(coord.min(), coord.max() + width, width)
    idx = np.clip(np.digitize(coord, edges) - 1, 0, len(edges) - 2)
    n = np.bincount(idx, minlength=len(edges) - 1)
    total = np.bincount(idx, weights=values, minlength=len(edges) - 1)
    mean = np.divide(total, n, out=np.full(len(n), np.nan), where=n >= min_cells)
    return edges[:-1] + width / 2, mean


def column_starts(edge, gap=100):
    """Where each column (or row) of fields of view starts: edges within `gap` µm are one."""
    v = np.sort(edge.round(-1).unique())
    return np.array([s for i, s in enumerate(v) if i == 0 or s - v[i - 1] > gap])


fov = pd.read_csv(FOV_EXTENTS, index_col="fov")
fov_size = float(np.median(fov.x_max - fov.x_min))
x_starts, y_starts = column_starts(fov.x_min), column_starts(fov.y_min)
x_bounds = np.sort(np.concatenate([x_starts, x_starts + fov_size]))
y_bounds = np.sort(np.concatenate([y_starts, y_starts + fov_size]))

plot_transcripts_on_tissue(
    xy, transcripts, np.quantile(transcripts, 0.99),
    mean_by_bin(xy[:, 0], transcripts), mean_by_bin(xy[:, 1], transcripts),
    x_bounds, y_bounds,
)
plt.show()
print(f"{len(fov)} fields of view, about {fov_size:.0f} µm square")
```


# Phase C — Filtering and dimension reduction

One default recipe, run on every section and left untuned. Nothing is clustered: cells are
annotated one at a time in Phase D, and the UMAP below is for looking at the data.

## C1. Filter cells

Drop cells under `LOW_COUNT_CUT` transcripts, the cut marked in B2. The high cut for doublets
and merged cells is off. All 491 genes are kept: the panel is already curated, so there is no
highly-variable-gene selection and no gene filter.

```{python}
n_before = adata.n_obs
sc.pp.filter_cells(adata, min_counts=LOW_COUNT_CUT)
print(f"kept {adata.n_obs:,} of {n_before:,} cells ({1 - adata.n_obs / n_before:.1%} dropped), "
      f"{adata.n_vars} genes")
```

## C2. Normalize

Scale every cell to the section's median total, then take the log. The log-normalized values
are kept in a layer, because scaling overwrites `X` and the markers in Phase D are read from
them.

```{python}
sc.pp.normalize_total(adata)
sc.pp.log1p(adata)
adata.layers["lognorm"] = adata.X.copy()
```

## C3. Scale

Unit variance, not centred, clipped at 10.

```{python}
sc.pp.scale(adata, zero_center=False, max_value=10)
```

## C4. PCA

Thirty components. The plot shows whether 30 is enough: the curve should be flat well before
the last component.

```{python}
sc.pp.pca(adata, n_comps=30, random_state=0)

variance_ratio = adata.uns["pca"]["variance_ratio"]
plot_pca_variance(variance_ratio, SAMPLE)
plt.show()
print(f"30 PCs explain {variance_ratio.sum():.1%} of the variance")
```

## C5. Neighbour graph

Fifteen neighbours, cosine distance.

```{python}
sc.pp.neighbors(adata, n_neighbors=15, metric="cosine", random_state=0)
```

## C6. UMAP

Coloured by transcript count, to show whether the structure follows how deeply a cell was
read rather than what it is. A gradient across one region is depth; a split into separate
islands is not.

```{python}
sc.tl.umap(adata, random_state=0)

plot_umap_by_count(
    adata.obsm["X_umap"], adata.obs["transcript_count"].to_numpy(),
    np.quantile(adata.obs["transcript_count"], 0.99), SAMPLE,
)
plt.show()
```

# Phase D — Cell-type annotation

Every cell is correlated against a reference and takes the type it correlates with most. The
first pass stops at germ or somatic: a cell is germ when that type is one of the four germ
types, and somatic otherwise. Nothing is clustered, and nothing is named at the cluster level.
Germ stage is left to a later step on the germ cells alone.

## D0. The reference

Green et al. 2018's 11 major cell types, as the mean expression per type over the panel genes:
ln(mean TP10K + 1). The table is made once for every section from the published counts and
labels (`NOTEBOOK.md` has the recipe) and is always there to load. The notebook never builds
it: a missing file is an error, since building it silently would take minutes and could differ
from the table every other section used.

```{python}
reference_file = REFERENCE_DIR / "green_major.csv"
if not reference_file.exists():
    raise FileNotFoundError(f"{reference_file} is missing; the reference is an input and is not built here")

reference = pd.read_csv(reference_file, index_col=0)[CELL_TYPES]
print(f"reference: {reference.shape[0]} genes x {reference.shape[1]} types")
```

## D3. Per-cell correlation

Spearman correlation of each cell's raw counts against every reference type, over the genes
the panel and the reference share. Spearman is Pearson on ranks, so both sides are ranked
across genes and correlated with one matrix product.

```{python}
shared = [gene for gene in adata.var_names if gene in reference.index]
shared_idx = adata.var_names.get_indexer(shared)


def spearman_to_reference(counts, ref):
    """Spearman correlation of each row of counts (cells x genes) with each column of ref (genes x types)."""

    def centred_ranks(x):
        ranks = rankdata(x, axis=1)
        ranks = ranks - ranks.mean(axis=1, keepdims=True)
        return ranks / np.linalg.norm(ranks, axis=1, keepdims=True)

    return centred_ranks(counts) @ centred_ranks(ref.T.to_numpy()).T


counts_shared = np.asarray(adata.layers["counts"])[:, shared_idx].astype(np.float32)
correlation = spearman_to_reference(counts_shared, reference.loc[shared])

plot_shared_genes(adata.n_vars, len(shared))
plt.show()
print(f"{correlation.shape[0]:,} cells x {correlation.shape[1]} types; "
      f"correlations run from {correlation.min():.2f} to {correlation.max():.2f}")
```

## D4. Standardize within each cell

A cell's correlation to every type rises with how many genes it captured. Standardizing each
cell's 11 correlations to zero mean and unit variance makes cells comparable with each other,
and cannot change which type is highest for any cell.

```{python}
standardized = (correlation - correlation.mean(axis=1, keepdims=True)) / correlation.std(axis=1, keepdims=True)
for j, cell_type in enumerate(reference.columns):
    adata.obs[f"corr_{cell_type}"] = standardized[:, j]
```

## D5. Per-cell call

The type each cell correlates with most, and from it germ or somatic: germ when the type is
SPG, Scytes, STids or Elongating. Drawn on the UMAP, the germ cells lie along one arc in stage
order, from Scytes through STids to Elongating, and the somatic types sit on a separate island.
On the tissue the germ cells fall inside the tubules in rings, with Scytes outermost and
Elongating nearest the lumen, and the somatic cells between them.

```{python}
adata.obs["cell_type"] = pd.Categorical(reference.columns.to_numpy()[standardized.argmax(axis=1)],
                                        categories=CELL_TYPES)
adata.obs["germ_somatic"] = pd.Categorical(np.where(adata.obs["cell_type"].isin(GERM), "germ", "somatic"),
                                           categories=["germ", "somatic"])

umap = adata.obsm["X_umap"]
tissue_xy = np.asarray(adata.obsm["spatial"])

plot_calls(umap, tissue_xy, adata.obs["cell_type"].astype(str), TYPE_COLORS, SAMPLE, "per-cell type")
plt.show()
print(adata.obs["cell_type"].value_counts().to_string())
```

The same calls, collapsed to germ and somatic. Somatic cells are drawn on top, since they are
the smaller group and would otherwise be buried.

```{python}
plot_calls(umap, tissue_xy, adata.obs["germ_somatic"].astype(str), GROUP_COLORS, SAMPLE,
           "germ vs somatic", last=["somatic"])
plt.show()
share = adata.obs["germ_somatic"].value_counts(normalize=True)
print(f"germ {share['germ']:.1%}, somatic {share['somatic']:.1%}")
```


## D6. Germ-cell subtypes

The germ cells alone, against Green's twelve germ-cell clusters, GC1 to GC12, as published. The
steps are D3 to D5 again on a finer reference: Spearman correlation of each germ cell's raw
counts, standardized within the cell, then its top cluster. Nothing is reclustered. GC1 to GC12
are differentiation states in order, so on tissue they should run from the wall inward.

```{python}
gc_file = REFERENCE_DIR / "green_gc.csv"
if not gc_file.exists():
    raise FileNotFoundError(f"{gc_file} is missing; the reference is an input and is not built here")

gc_reference = pd.read_csv(gc_file, index_col=0)[GC_TYPES]
gc_shared = [gene for gene in adata.var_names if gene in gc_reference.index]
gc_idx = adata.var_names.get_indexer(gc_shared)

is_germ = (adata.obs["germ_somatic"] == "germ").to_numpy()
germ_counts = np.asarray(adata.layers["counts"])[is_germ][:, gc_idx].astype(np.float32)
gc_corr = spearman_to_reference(germ_counts, gc_reference.loc[gc_shared])
gc_std = (gc_corr - gc_corr.mean(axis=1, keepdims=True)) / gc_corr.std(axis=1, keepdims=True)

adata.obs["germ_cluster"] = pd.Categorical([None] * adata.n_obs, categories=GC_TYPES)
adata.obs.loc[is_germ, "germ_cluster"] = np.array(GC_TYPES)[gc_std.argmax(axis=1)]
for j, gc in enumerate(GC_TYPES):
    adata.obs[f"corr_{gc}"] = np.nan
    adata.obs.loc[is_germ, f"corr_{gc}"] = gc_std[:, j]

gc_calls = adata.obs["germ_cluster"].astype(str).where(is_germ, "not germ")
plot_calls(umap, tissue_xy, gc_calls, GC_COLORS, SAMPLE, "germ-cell cluster", last=GC_TYPES)
plt.show()
print(f"{len(gc_shared)} of {adata.n_vars} panel genes shared with GC1-12")
print(adata.obs["germ_cluster"].value_counts().sort_index().to_string())
```

How the germ cells' major type and their cluster line up. Each row is a major type from D5 and
each cell is the share of that type's cells calling that cluster. SPG should sit in the low
clusters, Scytes in the middle and Elongating in the high ones.

```{python}
overlap = pd.crosstab(adata.obs.loc[is_germ, "cell_type"].astype(str),
                      adata.obs.loc[is_germ, "germ_cluster"].astype(str),
                      normalize="index").reindex(index=GERM, columns=GC_TYPES, fill_value=0)
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 3), constrained_layout=True)
image = ax.imshow(overlap.to_numpy(), cmap="viridis", aspect="auto")
ax.set_xticks(range(12), GC_TYPES)
ax.set_yticks(range(len(GERM)), GERM)
ax.set_title(f"{SAMPLE}: germ-cell cluster within each major germ type")
fig.colorbar(image, ax=ax, label="share of the type's cells")
plt.show()
```


# Phase E — Identify tubules

Every cell gets a tubule, or none. The tubules are Alex Vargo's: his boundaries were traced from
the Cellbound3 and DAPI images, and he assigned each cell to the tubule whose boundary contains
its centre. This notebook takes his cell-to-tubule map and his per-tubule table as inputs and
does not redo the segmentation.

## E1. Cell-to-tubule map

The map has one entry per cell of the section's table, in the table's order, and none for a cell
outside every tubule. C1 dropped cells, so each cell's position in the full table, kept in B1 as
`table_row`, picks out its entry. Tubule ids are kept as strings, with an empty string for no
tubule.

```{python}
cell_map = np.load(TUBULE_MAP, allow_pickle=True)["cell_map"]
assert len(cell_map) == N_TABLE_CELLS, "the map is not indexed by this section's table"

assigned = cell_map[adata.obs["table_row"].to_numpy()]
adata.obs["tubule_id"] = np.array(["" if t is None else str(t) for t in assigned], dtype=object)
adata.obs["in_tubule"] = (adata.obs["tubule_id"] != "").to_numpy()

print(f"{adata.obs['in_tubule'].sum():,} of {adata.n_obs:,} cells are in a tubule "
      f"({adata.obs['in_tubule'].mean():.0%}); {adata.obs.loc[adata.obs['in_tubule'], 'tubule_id'].nunique()} tubules")
```

## E2. Tubule table

One row per tubule: his metadata (a quality flag for the cells, whether the outline is a good
circle, and its area, eccentricity and major axis length, in mosaic pixels), with the number of
cells in the tubule and the share of them that are germ.

```{python}
tubule_meta = pd.read_csv(TUBULE_META, index_col=0)
tubule_meta.index = tubule_meta.index.astype(str)

inside = adata.obs[adata.obs["in_tubule"]]
per_tubule = pd.DataFrame({
    "n_cells": inside.groupby("tubule_id").size(),
    "germ_share": (inside["germ_somatic"] == "germ").groupby(inside["tubule_id"]).mean(),
})
tubules = per_tubule.join(tubule_meta, how="left")

print(f"{len(tubules)} tubules; {tubules['good_cells_bin'].sum()} flagged good for cells; "
      f"{tubules['good_circle'].sum()} with a good circular outline; "
      f"{tubules['good_cells_bin'].isna().sum()} with no metadata row")
tubules.head()
```

## E3. Check the assignment

Each tubule in its own colour, with the somatic cells outside any tubule in grey and the germ
cells outside in black. Germ cells should be inside tubules, so black marks tubules that have no
outline or tissue the images did not cover. His boundaries are generous, taking in some of the
space between tubules, so some interstitial cells land inside a tubule as well; the share of each
cell type inside shows how many.

```{python}
codes = pd.factorize(adata.obs["tubule_id"].replace("", np.nan))[0]   # -1 where there is no tubule
is_germ = (adata.obs["germ_somatic"] == "germ").to_numpy()

plot_tubules_on_tissue(tissue_xy, codes, is_germ, SAMPLE)
plt.show()
```

```{python}
share_inside = adata.obs.groupby("cell_type", observed=True)["in_tubule"].mean()

plot_tubule_qc(tubules["n_cells"].to_numpy(), share_inside)
plt.show()
print(f"germ cells inside a tubule: {adata.obs.loc[is_germ, 'in_tubule'].mean():.1%}; "
      f"somatic: {adata.obs.loc[~is_germ, 'in_tubule'].mean():.1%}")
```


# Phase G — Tubule stage

Each tubule cross-section sits at one stage of the epithelial cycle. The stages used here are
Alex Vargo's: he staged tubules by eye from per-tubule images, into four groups, and the calls are
in the tubule metadata of the sections he staged. A section without them skips this phase and the
next, and a staging for those sections is built later.

## G1. Staged tubules

The tubules with a stage in one of the four groups, flagged by him as good for cells. A few
sections also have finer values, such as `3-4` or `7`, which are left out and counted.

```{python}
STAGED = "stage" in tubules.columns

if STAGED:
    good = tubules["good_cells_bin"] == True
    in_groups = tubules["stage"].isin(STAGE_GROUPS)
    staged = tubules[good & in_groups].copy()
    staged["stage"] = pd.Categorical(staged["stage"], STAGE_GROUPS, ordered=True)
    print(f"{len(staged)} of {len(tubules)} tubules are staged and good for cells; "
          f"{(good & tubules['stage'].notna() & ~in_groups).sum()} have a finer stage and are left out")
    print(staged["stage"].value_counts().sort_index().to_string())
else:
    print("this section has no stage calls; Phases G and H are skipped")
```

# Phase H — Within the tubule, by stage

## H1. Cell-type proportions by stage

Each cell type's share of the cells in a tubule, by stage group. His staging does not depend on
our calls, so the germ composition is not circular here. A Kruskal-Wallis test per type asks
whether a type's share differs between the groups; the p values are not corrected for the number
of types. The interstitial types that land inside a tubule's outline do not vary with stage: they
are cells inside generous boundaries, not residents of the tubule.

```{python}
if STAGED:
    inside = adata.obs[adata.obs["in_tubule"]]
    composition = (
        pd.crosstab(inside["tubule_id"], inside["cell_type"].astype(str), normalize="index")
        .reindex(columns=CELL_TYPES, fill_value=0)
        .loc[staged.index]
    )
    mean_composition = composition.groupby(staged["stage"], observed=True).mean()

    summary = pd.DataFrame({
        cell_type: {**{g: f"{mean_composition.loc[g, cell_type]:.1%}" for g in STAGE_GROUPS},
                    "Kruskal p": f"{kruskal(*[composition.loc[staged['stage'] == g, cell_type] for g in STAGE_GROUPS]).pvalue:.1e}"}
        for cell_type in CELL_TYPES
    }).T
    print(summary.to_string())

    plot_stage_composition(mean_composition, staged["stage"].value_counts(), SAMPLE)
    plt.show()
```

## H2. Cell density by stage

A share changes whenever the other types change. Cells per 10,000 µm² of the tubule's outline
separate the two. The outline includes the lumen, so a density mixes how tightly cells are packed
with how large the lumen is.

```{python}
if STAGED:
    counts = (
        pd.crosstab(inside["tubule_id"], inside["cell_type"].astype(str))
        .reindex(columns=CELL_TYPES, fill_value=0)
        .loc[staged.index]
    )
    area_um2 = staged["area"] * UM_PER_PX**2
    density = counts.div(area_um2, axis=0) * 1e4
    density["germ"] = density[GERM].sum(axis=1)
    density["all cells"] = density[CELL_TYPES].sum(axis=1)

    shown = GERM + ["Sertoli", "germ", "all cells"]
    medians = density.groupby(staged["stage"], observed=True)[shown].median().T
    medians["Kruskal p"] = [
        f"{kruskal(*[density.loc[staged['stage'] == g, column] for g in STAGE_GROUPS]).pvalue:.1e}" for column in shown
    ]
    print("median cells per 10,000 µm²:")
    print(medians.round(1).to_string())

    plot_stage_density(density, staged["stage"], GERM + ["Sertoli", "all cells"], SAMPLE)
    plt.show()
```
